product.name: Secrets
promise: Read only by the workload that may.
product.lede: Secrets keeps the tokens and keys a workload holds on a person's behalf. A workload hands it a value; Secrets encrypts it in the application, stores only ciphertext in PostgreSQL, and gives it back only to a workload granted that exact tenant and action. The person who owns it can see its metadata, revoke it or delete it, and nobody reads a value back through a user route.
product.meta: Rust service and client · PostgreSQL · specified in ESS · Apache-2.0

sections.title: Custody, not provider logic.
sections.lede: Secrets holds bytes, versions, ownership and audit records. OAuth exchange, refresh and upstream revocation stay in the service that integrates the provider.

items.title: Encrypted before storage
items.description: Every version gets its own data key, wrapped by a versioned key-encryption key that PostgreSQL never sees. The ciphertext is bound to its tenant, reference, version and disclosure.

items.title: Tenant-bound, least privilege
items.description: Workloads are Kubernetes service accounts granted explicit actions in one tenant; people are verified by Identity and act only on what they own.

items.title: Atomic prepared batches
items.description: A workload stages puts and deletes in one tenant and commits them in one PostgreSQL transaction, or aborts them.

items.title: Named secrets over several backends
items.description: An in-process library with named, scoped secrets over the OS keychain, read-only 1Password and this service, and a CLI that never prints a secret.

sections.title: From request to ciphertext.
sections.lede: Every route follows the same order: the caller is verified before storage is touched, and the value is encrypted before it reaches the database.

steps.label: HTTP
steps.title: Bounded request
steps.description: A JSON body of at most 1 MiB and a bearer token. Values travel only in bodies.

steps.label: Authority
steps.title: Verify the caller
steps.description: Kubernetes TokenReview for workloads, Identity for people: subject, tenant and actions.

steps.label: Policy
steps.title: Check tenant and action
steps.description: The route's action and the request's tenant must match the principal, or it is refused.

steps.label: Crypto
steps.title: Seal the value
steps.description: A fresh data key, AES-256-GCM, wrapped by the active key with the reference as associated data.

steps.label: PostgreSQL
steps.title: Commit with its audit row
steps.description: Ciphertext, wrapped key, metadata and one audit event in one transaction.

sections.title: What Secrets is specified in.
sections.lede: The secrets.custody domain of the ESS specification, retrofitted from the shipped service. A conformance suite of 111 scenarios runs it against the real router and store on every check. Generated from spec/ by secrets-docs.
